sentences.text: This appeal having been heard and reserved for orders, coming on for pronouncement this day, JUSTICE AVANINDRA KUMAR SINGH passed the following:

ORDER This appeal has been filed by the appellants who were claimants before Claims Tribunal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 assailing the award dated 17.05.2013 passed by learned IV th M.A.C.T., Chhatarpur in Motor Accident Claim Case No. 114/2011 on the ground that less compensation has been awarded regarding death of Latif Shah in the motor accident.
The income of the deceased has not been considered judiciously in spite of the pleadings and evidence available to the learned Tribunal.
The deceased used to get Rs. 10,000/- per month as salary and Rs. 50/- per day towards meals allowance.

The Tribunal also applied erroneously multiplier of 13 instead of 18 as at the time of death of deceased he was of 28 years, therefore, award is liable to be enhanced by a further sum of Rs.5,00,000/- along with interest at the rate of 12% per annum from the date of filing of claim application i.e. 24.10.2011.
2. None appeared for the respondents, in spite of service.
3. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant.
Perused the record.
The question before this Court is whether compensation can be enhanced, on the grounds urged in this appeal.
4. Thus, the first ground is regarding the salary of deceased per month.
In the claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, the father of deceased Ashok Shah has filed an affidavit under Order 18 Rule 4 of C.P.C.

In Para 9 of cross-examination, he (Ashok Shah) has admitted that he has not filed any document to show that the deceased Latif was working in Sujat Travels and was earning Rs. 10,000/- per month as salary along with Rs. 50/- per day for meal.
He further admitted in para-10 that Latif was not married.
5. Applicant witness No. 3 (Saif Ullah Khan) has also filed an affidavit under Order 18 Rule 4 of C.P.C. and has stated that Latif Shah was given Rs.5000/- per month salary.
In Para 4 of cross-examination, this witness has accepted that he has not filed any return showing payment made to the employees.
Further, he does not recruit or relieve employees on the basis of orders on his letter pad.
He further admitted in Para-5 that there is no receipt showing payment has been made to the deceased.

In fact, Ex. P- 8 is a document which was issued after the death of Latif Shah,
therefore, ground of the appellants that their son was getting Rs. 10,000/- per month salary is contradicted by their own witness i.e. Saif Ullah Khan.

2 6.
The learned Claims Tribunal has treated deceased as an unskilled worker and assessed his income as Rs.3,000/- per month.

As per record of the claim petition, the accident in which deceased expired, took place on 03.09.2011, in Chhatarpur City and on said date the minimum wage of an unskilled worker in Madhya Pradesh was Rs.3,070/- per month, therefore, on this ground suitable enhancement can be made in the award.
Similarly, the age of deceased as recorded in the postmortem report (Ex. A-3) is 28 years.
There is no other document from which, some other age can be ascertained.

The multiplier applied by the learned Tribunal is not as per the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Sarla Verma and ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation and anr.
2009 ACJ 1298 SC and as per the judgment dated 14.08.2019 of Hon'ble the Supreme Court in Joginder Singh and anr. v. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company (2020) 18 SCC 808 in which it is held that, it is the age of deceased, and not parents which is relevant for applying the correct multiplier.

sentences.text: The applicable multiplier in the instant case would be 17 and not 13, as has been applied by the learned Tribunal.

Therefore, the calculation of compensation would be as follows :-
Rs. 3,070 per month x 12 = Rs. 36,840/- (per annum) Rs. 36,840 x 17 (multiplier) =
Rs. 6,26,280/-
Rs. 6,26,280 x 130/100 = Rs. 8,14,164/- (on adding towards future prospects 30%)
7.
As the deceased was unmarried, therefore, the parents would be entitled only to 50% of amount of compensation.
It is presumed that rest of the amount would be spent by the deceased on himself or his future family.
Therefore, the amount of compensation to claimants would become Rs. 8,14,164 / 2 = Rs.4,07,082/-.
In this amount, if we add Rs.15,000/- for loss of estate, and Rs.15,000/- for funeral expenses, the amount would come to Rs.4,37,082/- .

In this Rs.80,000/- can be given to the claimants/parents on account of loss of filial consortium, as per judgment of Hon'ble the Supreme Court Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others (2018) 18 SCC 130, therefore,
amount would become Rs.5,17,082/-.
8.

entities.text: Supreme Court Magma General Insurance Company Limited vs. Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram and others (2018) 18 SCC 130
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed and it is directed to the insurance company to pay additional amount of Rs.1,97,882/- (Rs.
5,17,082/- - Rs.3,19,200/-) to the appellants/claimants.
As regards the rate of interest i.e. 7.5%, it does not require any interference.
9. Accordingly, the appeal is partly allowed to the extent indicated above.
